questions.question: Why is 'Be helpful and concise' a weak system prompt rule?
options: It can't be tested: there's no clear pass or fail
questions.explanation: A rule you can't check can't be enforced or regression-tested.

questions.question: Which is the most testable version of a length rule?
questions.explanation: It maps directly to a check: len(reply.split()) < 60.

questions.question: Why give the exact out-of-scope reply in the prompt?
options: So refusals are consistent and an automatic check can recognise them
questions.explanation: An exact string makes both 'refused correctly' and 'refused wrongly' measurable.

questions.question: The first live run scored 75/75. What did reading the replies reveal?
options: The checks missed an invented '24-48 hours' and an in-scope question being refused
questions.explanation: A perfect score from unread outputs usually means weak checks.

questions.question: The contract prompt refused an in-scope returns question in 4 of 5 runs. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Tight scopes can make models decline things they're allowed to do. Test for it explicitly.

questions.question: On the checks both prompts could pass, the vague prompt scored 77/105 and the contract 100/105. What's the next step?
options: Fix the over-refusal (e.g. an in-scope example), then re-run the whole suite to catch regressions
Go back to the vague prompt
questions.explanation: One edit at a time, re-run everything, keep the scores.
